why: The 60 Hz half of the density calibration's bad side, measured after the PR 1361 review ran the experiment ADR-0145 admitted was missing and falsified its narrowing. The ADR-0135-rejected Appium UiAutomator2 browser transport, driven against the 60 Hz emulator: BOTH runs measure 0.82 moves/frame with gap p95 22 ms (passing the 0.6-floor gate as shipped), and the distortion is a per-run lottery - run A reports a fake 6.84% in-contact lost with the engine at 0.11 ms/frame (the coupled script channel stalling the main thread), run B a genuinely clean 0.00%. No input tail statistic separates A from healthy captures (A's move-gap max is 120 ms; the healthy corpus holds a real 351 ms pause), which is why the fix raises the density floor to 0.9 - bad side 0.82 across five runs (three in the PR 1361 review thread, these two banked) against the healthy floor of 0.96 - and removes this transport from the emulator's campaign plan entirely.
